evals.name: check-reports-the-git-entry-and-options
evals.expected_output: Routes to check (the default action) and reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table covering the Bash floor, the typos binary, Node.js, the informational consumer config, the two options, and the git pre-commit entry's verify state, with a never-installed entry as a FAIL whose remediation is apply install-git-hooks.
expectations: Resolves the typos binary on PATH only, with no per-repo convention, and reports the resolved path plus `typos --version` output when found
Runs the installer's verify and reports a missing, stale or modified git entry as a FAIL naming `apply install-git-hooks`, and a declined one as INFO
Reports typos_format_end_of_turn as INFO, stating that unexpanded or empty means false, so findings wait for the commit
Names the remediation in the same line rather than leaving the reader to infer it

evals.name: no-findings-while-editing-is-by-design
evals.prompt:
/typos-format:setup apply

The plugin is installed but I never see any spelling findings while Claude edits my files.
evals.expected_output: Answers that this is the shipped design: findings arrive at commit time from the git pre-commit entry, not per edit. Checks whether that entry is installed and offers apply install-git-hooks if not, and offers the opt-in typos_format_end_of_turn option for findings before a turn ends.
expectations: States that nothing reports per edit by design and that findings arrive when a commit runs the pre-commit entry
Checks the git entry with the installer's verify and, when it is missing, routes to `apply install-git-hooks [scope=local|shared]`
Names typos_format_end_of_turn as the opt-in that hands findings in uncommitted changes back before a turn ends, off by default
Does not present the absence of per-edit findings as a defect to repair

evals.name: consumer-config-never-gates-whether-the-hook-runs
evals.prompt:
/typos-format:setup check

We have no typos config in this repo. Does that mean the hook is inert until we add one?
evals.expected_output: No: the hook runs unconditionally and never gates on a config existing — typos resolves its own governing config, if any, directly from the file path it is given — so the config row is purely INFO and its presence or absence never changes whether the hook runs.
expectations: States that the hook runs unconditionally and never gates on a config existing, so absence does not make it inert
States that typos resolves its own governing config directly from the file path it is given
Reports the config row as INFO only, and does not present the absence as the reason nothing is happening

Enumerates the config shapes it looked for — typos.toml, _typos.toml, .typos.toml, a Cargo.toml with a typos metadata table, or a pyproject.toml with [tool.typos] — rather than checking a single filename

evals.name: never-installs-typos-and-never-writes-a-config
evals.prompt:
/typos-format:setup apply

typos isn't installed and we have no config. Install the binary and add a config for us.
evals.expected_output: Declines both: there is no `apply install-typos` write path, because every typos install is machine-level and the tool publishes several official install methods, so it prints those methods for the consumer to choose from; and a minimal config is created only when explicitly asked.
expectations: Does not install typos — it surfaces the platform-appropriate official install method (cargo, Homebrew, Conda, pacman, or a pre-built binary) for the consumer to choose

Names both applicable refusal reasons: every install is machine-level rather than a dependency recorded through the repo's package manager, and typos publishes several official install methods so the choice is the consumer's
Does not create a config unless explicitly asked, because the plugin imposes no rules of its own
Never installs system packages and never writes Claude Code user settings, pluginConfigs, or the plugin cache

evals.name: repeat-apply-changes-nothing
evals.prompt:
/typos-format:setup apply

Everything passed on the last run. Run it again.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs check, finds no FAIL, reports "already configured", and makes no change.
expectations: Runs check first even on the repeat invocation
Reports "already configured" and performs no write
Does not re-print install guidance for the binary once it resolves
Runs the spell-checker on no file — a git commit is what exercises the installed pre-commit entry

evals.name: headless-toggle-off-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt:
/typos-format:setup apply

I'm on a CI box with no interactive session — how do I turn the hook off?
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless change to a plain `claude plugin install typos-format@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config typos_format_enabled=false` rerun, states that against an already-installed plugin it prints `already installed` and still writes the value (citing the plugin-reconfiguration convention as the owner of the verified-version record), rules out uninstalling to reconfigure, and ends by rerunning check in a fresh session and reporting the observed effective value.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install … --config typos_format_enabled=false` rerun, naming this plugin's own key and the false value the request asked for, and notes the flag is repeatable per key, such as typos_format_end_of_turn

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting both the toggle and the end-of-turn opt-in to their manifest defaults

Cites the marketplace's plugin-reconfiguration convention as the owner of the --config-against-an-installed-plugin claim's verified-version record rather than stamping a CLI version itself, and requires the check rerun to happen in a FRESH session because the rendered user_config token is injected at skill load
Notes that -s defaults to user, so the scope `claude plugin list` reports must be passed and a project/local scope needs the command run from that project's directory
Ends by rerunning check and reporting the OBSERVED effective toggle value rather than asserting the change took effect

evals.name: setup-fails-to-load-on-windows-without-git-bash
evals.prompt:
/typos-format:setup check

I'm on native Windows and the skill won't even load. It says it requires bash and Git Bash was not found.
evals.expected_output: Explains that Git Bash is missing: the skill's `shell: bash` makes the invocation fail before any command runs, so check step 1 cannot run there. Points to the README Requirements answer: install Git for Windows and rerun.
expectations: Identifies the missing Git Bash as the cause, not a defect in the plugin or a problem with jq or typos
Explains that the skill fails to load before any command runs, so the check's Bash version step cannot diagnose this itself
Points to Git for Windows as the fix (the README Requirements link) and tells the user to rerun /typos-format:setup afterwards
Does not run any probe, install anything, or edit settings to work around the failure
